Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Parallel Computer Architecture [NPT_4132]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain how Flynn's taxonomy can be extended to classify modern heterogeneous architectures.        (5)  
  Discuss its limitations in today's context  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Analyze the trade-offs between UMA and NUMA architectures in large-scale multiprocessors. How       (5)  
  do these choices affect memory latency and programmability?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Demonstrate how the message-passing model can be used to compute the matrix-vector product          (5)  
  on a 4-node cluster. Show the data distribution and communication pattern.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)           Analyze the role of the VI protocol as a baseline coherence mechanism. How does its simplicity      (5)  
  help in reasoning about correctness compared to more complex protocols like MESI?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
3)                Assess how coherence correctness like write serialization, data consistency, and atomicity is      (5)  
  maintained in Dragon and MESI protocols. Discuss failure scenarios that could violate correctness.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Develop an evaluation framework to measure coherence performance in a multicore system with         (5)  
  single vs. multi-level caches. Identify metrics that reflect both latency and traffic efficiency  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                Compare directory-based coherence to snooping protocols for large-scale multiprocessors in terms (5)  
  of scalability, fault tolerance, and hardware complexity. Provide design reasoning for preferring one  
  A)           in NUMA systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Evaluate the Sequent NUMA-Q architecture's coherence protocol for correctness and latency.          (5)  
  Propose a hybrid coherence approach combining snooping and directory methods for improved  
  performance.  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5)                        Analyze the trade-offs between strict consistency and release consistency in parallel systems.       (5)  
  Discuss how synchronization primitives help enforce ordering under relaxed models.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)                Evaluate the performance implications of point-to-point synchronization versus global barriers in    (5)  
  NUMA architectures. Suggest design improvements to reduce synchronization overhead.?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
